prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) NextGen/National Airspace System (NAS); National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Airspace Technology Demonstrations 3 (ATD-3). Actors: FAA managers/controllers, airline air traffic control (ATC) coordinators/dispatchers, aircraft/operators/pilots/crews, American Airlines. Traffic Management Initiatives (TMIs) divert/meter; managers designate Flow Constrained Areas (FCAs). Severe Weather Avoidance Plans (SWAP)=Playbook routes, 2–8-hour horizon. Dispatchers must file ≥45 minutes pre-pushback. Collaborative Trajectory Options Program (CTOP) receives operator route/delay preferences; no postdeparture optimization.
NASA Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR), extending Direct-To, continuously analyzes flights ≥10,000 ft using tracks/plans/weather/airspace/traffic. Maneuver Start Point (MSP): adjustable coordination delay (default five minutes) or altitude entry (Fort Worth Center=ZFW: FL240); snaps within 10 nmi. Return Capture Fix (RCF; Capture fix): last fix within limit rectangle (~200 nmi beyond ZFW), or before Standard Terminal Arrival Route (STAR). Historical clearance polygons: Future ATM Concept Evaluation Tool (FACET)/National Airspace System Constraint Evaluation and Notification Tool (NASCENT). Wind-corrected savings threshold defaults to five minutes. Weather/optional-traffic avoidance inserts one/two minimum-delay auxiliary waypoints. Both trajectories checked for congestion/Special Use Airspace (SUA); weather/traffic conflicts reject trials. DWR sends qualifying advisories to responsible users’ savings-ordered list. Indicators: TR=traffic minutes-to-conflict; SC=sector congestion; WX=weather; R=active Route TMI. Users drag route points; controller coordination required. Digital ATC–flight-deck route exchange/onboard display could accelerate approval.
FAA Corridor Integrated Weather System (CIWS) forecasts cell growth/decay/movement: five-minute updates/increments, two-hour horizon. Convective Weather Avoidance Model (CWAM) produces Weather Avoidance Field (WAF) polygons: historical crew-deviation probabilities based on intensity, echo tops, look-ahead; 60/70/80%, FL250–FL450 every 1,000 ft. DWR predicts weather clearance at passage; normally uses 70% WAF, configurable at startup. Gap detection/rejection ensures safe passage.

New part:
U0126: This function includes a distance buffer that will reject a route amendment if it will go through a gap that is narrower than 50nm laterally (user-adjustable parameter) either side of route and 75nm longitudinally (user-adjustable parameter) to the predicted cells at the time the aircraft reaches the point closest to the cells (see Figure 9).
U0127: If convective cells are predicted to encroach on one side of a trajectory but not on the other, (blue polygons in left graphic of Figure 9) it is generally not considered an operational problem because there is room for flight crews to maneuver around the cell.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
